issues.legal_issue: A person whose property interest is not affected by an evacuee-property declaration cannot challenge that declaration.
material_facts: The petitioners were not evacuees and held shares in the properties.
The declaration identified only the shares of family members who had migrated as evacuee property.
The declaration did not purport to affect the petitioners’ shares.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners could not challenge the declaration, and the Court did not decide whether the notice underlying it was valid.
issues.legal_principle: A person cannot challenge an order in proceedings that did not purport to affect that person’s interest. Because the declaration affected only the evacuees’ shares, the petitioners were not concerned with its validity.

predicates.constitutional_property_challenge: A claimant brings a constitutional proceeding to challenge an order concerning property.
predicates.declaration_limited_to_others_interests: The order declares only the interests of other persons to be evacuee property.
predicates.claimant_interest_unaffected: The order does not purport to affect the claimant’s property interest.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a constitutional property challenge, the order concerns only others’ interests, and the claimant’s own interest is unaffected, the challenge is unavailable to that claimant.

issues.legal_issue: An order under the separation-of-interests regime cannot vest an entire property in the Custodian when the prior determination identified only a defined share as evacuee property.
material_facts: The Custodian had determined that the evacuees owned a four-sevenths share in the properties, rather than the entire properties.
The separation officer issued a notice to separate the evacuee interest, and no claim was filed.
The officer then ordered the entire properties to vest in the Custodian, including the shares of persons who were not evacuees.
issues.conclusion: The order vesting the entire properties in the Custodian was set aside; proper steps to separate the evacuee interest remained available.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(b), 2(d), 6, 8, 8(2), 10 and 11 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951, read together, provide for determining or separating the evacuee interest, not converting non-evacuee property into evacuee property. Section 8(2) makes the Custodian’s determination binding on the competent officer, while preserving the officer’s power to separate the interests under section 10. The Court relied on Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Tek Chand Dolwani, which held that property does not vest in the Custodian without proceedings under section 7 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950. Section 11 therefore does not authorize vesting the whole property where the prior determination found only a share to be evacuee property.

predicates.separation_proceeding: An officer is conducting proceedings to determine or separate an evacuee interest from other interests in property.
predicates.prior_determination_limited_evacuee_inte: The prior determination identifies only a defined share, and not the whole property, as evacuee property.
predicates.order_vested_entire_property: The officer orders the entire property, including non-evacuee interests, to vest in the Custodian.

issues.definition: In separation proceedings, when the prior determination identifies only a defined share as evacuee property but the officer orders the entire property to vest in the Custodian, the entire-property vesting order is invalid.
